verdict.rationale: Bitwarden's docs describe exporting the vault to back up data and importing from 'encrypted exports', so encrypted backups exist. A community user also calls it an e2ee password manager. The pack never documents that the vendor never holds the key, and it never shows the encryption design. Missing for 10: first-party zero-knowledge/key-custody documentation, a published encryption design (key derivation and ciphers), proof that exports and sync are end-to-end encrypted with user-held keys, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, backups are end-to-end encrypted with a key the vendor never holds, and the encryption design is documented

citations.quote: Import logins and data from different password managers, other Bitwarden vaults, or encrypted exports
Export your vault data, including logins and notes, to back up important information
I move to the next ethical e2ee password manager if BitWarden turns its back on open source
